For whatever Christ prayed for with deliberate reason and with the rational will taken simply [that is, the will as a power of reason, as distinct from his natural will of sense, which shrank from the passion], he obtained.

paras.t: Projecisti me in profundum in corde maris. Hoc est quod ait in Psalmo: Infixus sum in limo profundi; et, Veni in altitudinem maris. Istud ergo profundum, est, vel caro mortalis assumpta, vel inferiores partes terræ, in quas (Paulo teste) descendit Salvator. Porro cor maris est Judæa, in medio terræ habitabilis sita, quemadmodum cor est in medio animalis. Ibi enim operatus est nostram salutem. Circumdedit me flumen tentationum, persecutionum et passionum. Tota enim conversatio Christi in sæculo isto, quasi in abundantia tribulationum fuit, præsertim quum toties compassus fuerit mundo, et in paupertate præcipua vixit. Omnes gurgites tui et fluctus tui super me transierunt, id est, prædictis adversitatibus sum afflictus, opertus, probatus: quemadmodum dicit Apostolus, Non habemus pontificem qui non possit compati, sed probatum per omnia. Hinc Christus fatetur in Psalmo: Tempestas demersit me; et, Repleta est malis anima mea; ibidemque, Super me confirmatus est furor tuus, et omnes fluctus tuos induxisti super me. Hoc quoque aliquo modo dicere possunt in magnis et multis afflictionibus constituti, et cum Apostolo dicere possunt: Supra modum gravati sumus, supra virtutem. De talibus demum aquis et fluctibus scriptum est in Threnis: Inundaverunt aquæ super caput meum.
paras.en: [[2:4|thou hast cast me forth into the deep, in the heart of the sea|Projecisti me in profundum in corde maris]]. This is what he says in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:3|I stick fast in the mire of the deep|Infixus sum in limo profundi]]; and, [[Ps 68:3|I am come into the depth of the sea|Veni in altitudinem maris]]. This deep, then, is either the mortal flesh he took, or [[Eph 4:9|the lower parts of the earth|inferiores partes terræ]], into which (as Paul testifies) the Saviour descended. Further, the heart of the sea is Judæa, set in the middle of the habitable earth, as the heart is in the middle of an animal. For there he wrought our salvation[[Ps 73:12||]]. [[2:4|a flood hast compassed me|Circumdedit me flumen]]: a flood of temptations, persecutions and sufferings. For the whole life of Christ in this world was, as it were, in an abundance of tribulations, especially since he so often had compassion on the world, and lived in the utmost poverty. [[2:4|all thy billows, and thy waves have passed over me|Omnes gurgites tui et fluctus tui super me transierunt]], that is, I have been afflicted, covered and tried by the adversities just named: as the Apostle says, [[Heb 4:15|we have not a high priest who cannot have compassion|Non habemus pontificem qui non possit compati]], but one tried [[Heb 4:15|in all things|per omnia]] [Denis reads *probatum*, "tried", where the Vulgate has *tentatum*, "tempted"]. Hence Christ confesses in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:3|a tempest hath overwhelmed me|Tempestas demersit me]]; and, [[Ps 87:4|my soul is filled with evils|Repleta est malis anima mea]]; and in the same Psalm, [[Ps 87:8|Thy wrath is strong over me: and all thy waves thou hast brought in upon me|Super me confirmatus est furor tuus, et omnes fluctus tuos induxisti super me]]. This too those who are set in great and many afflictions can say in some manner, and they can say with the Apostle: [[2 Cor 1:8|we were pressed out of measure above our strength|Supra modum gravati sumus, supra virtutem]]. Finally, of such waters and waves it is written in Lamentations: [[Lam 3:54|Waters have flowed over my head|Inundaverunt aquæ super caput meum]].

paras.t: Et ego dixi in cruce: Abjectus sum a conspectu oculorum tuorum, quum dixi: Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me? Unde in Isaia legitur: Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo, et humiliatum. Non quod absolute relictus fuit a Deo, sed quoniam inferiori parti animæ subtracta fuit solita consolatio, et natura assumpta potestati tenebrarum et manibus impiorum exposita fuit, in tantum quod satiati sunt pœnis ejus. Sicque videbatur Christus homo abjectus a Deo. Ideo enim dixerunt: Si rex Israel est, vel, Si hic est Christus Dei electus, descendat nunc de cruce; confidit in Deo, liberet eum nunc, si vult. Verumtamen rursus videbo templum sanctum tuum, id est Apostolos et Ecclesiam militantem ac triumphantem. Hinc apud Joannem ait: Iterum autem videbo vos, et gaudebit cor vestrum. Unde cantatur in Psalmo: Confitebor tibi in Ecclesia magna; et, In medio Ecclesiæ laudabo te.
paras.en: [[2:5|And I said|Et ego dixi]] on the cross: [[2:5|I am cast away out of the sight of thy eyes|Abjectus sum a conspectu oculorum tuorum]], when I said: [[Matt 27:46|My God, My God, why hast thou forsaken me?|Deus meus, Deus meus, ut quid dereliquisti me?]][[Ps 21:2||]] Hence we read in Isaias: [[Is 53:4|we have thought him as it were a leper, and as one struck by God and afflicted|Nos putavimus eum quasi leprosum, et percussum a Deo, et humiliatum]]. Not that he was absolutely forsaken by God, but because the accustomed consolation was withdrawn from the lower part of his soul, and the nature he had taken was given over to the power of darkness and to the hands of the wicked, so far that they were filled with his pains[[Job 16:11||]]. And so Christ the man seemed cast away by God. For this is why they said: [[Matt 27:42|If he be the king of Israel|Si rex Israel est]], or, [[Luke 23:35|if he be Christ, the elect of God|Si hic est Christus Dei electus]], [[Matt 27:42|let him now come down from the cross|descendat nunc de cruce]]; [[Matt 27:43|He trusted in God: let him now deliver him if he will have him|confidit in Deo, liberet eum nunc, si vult]]. [[2:5|but yet I shall see the holy temple again|Verumtamen rursus videbo templum sanctum tuum]], that is, the Apostles and the Church militant and triumphant. Hence he says in John: [[John 16:22|I will see you again and your heart shall rejoice|Iterum autem videbo vos, et gaudebit cor vestrum]]. Hence it is sung in the Psalm: [[Ps 34:18|I will give thanks to thee in a great church|Confitebor tibi in Ecclesia magna]]; and, [[Ps 21:23|in the midst of the church will I praise thee|In medio Ecclesiæ laudabo te]].

paras.t: Circumdederunt me aquæ tribulationum usque ad animam, id est usque ad corporalis vitæ exstinctionem: juxta illud in Psalmo, Salvum me fac, Deus, quoniam intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam.
paras.en: [[2:6|The waters compassed me about|Circumdederunt me aquæ]], the waters of tribulations, [[2:6|even to the soul|usque ad animam]], that is, even to the extinction of bodily life: according to that in the Psalm, [[Ps 68:2|Save me, O God: for the waters are come in even unto my soul|Salvum me fac, Deus, quoniam intraverunt aquæ usque ad animam meam]].

paras.t: Ad extrema montium descendi secundum animam in puncto mortis, id est ad inferiora terræ loca; terræ vectes concluserunt me, ita quod infra portas inferni fui detentus spontanee, non arctatus, nec captus, aut proprie clausus; imo portas æreas contrivi, et vectes ferreos confregi. Judæi vero putabant eum una cum impiis in æternum damnatum, secundum quod Christus fatetur in Psalmo: Posuerunt me in lacu inferiori, in tenebrosis et in umbra mortis. Ideo subditur, in æternum. Et sublevabis de corruptione vitam meam: quoniam non dedisti Sanctum tuum videre corruptionem, et ad immortalem vitam suscitasti me tertio die.
paras.en: [[2:7|I went down to the lowest parts of the mountains|Ad extrema montium descendi]] in my soul at the moment of death, that is, to the lower places of the earth; [[2:7|the bars of the earth have shut me up|terræ vectes concluserunt me]], so that I was held beneath the gates of hell of my own will, not constrained, nor taken captive, nor properly shut in; nay rather, I have [[Ps 106:16|broken gates of brass, and burst iron bars|portas æreas contrivi, et vectes ferreos confregi]]. But the Jews thought him damned for ever along with the wicked, as Christ confesses in the Psalm: [[Ps 87:7|They have laid me in the lower pit: in the dark places, and in the shadow of death|Posuerunt me in lacu inferiori, in tenebrosis et in umbra mortis]]. Therefore it is added, [[2:7|for ever|in æternum]]. [[2:7|and thou wilt bring up my life from corruption|Et sublevabis de corruptione vitam meam]]: for thou didst not [[Ps 15:10|give thy holy one to see corruption|dedisti Sanctum tuum videre corruptionem]][[Acts 2:27||]], and thou didst raise me to immortal life on the third day.

paras.t: Quum angustiaretur in me anima mea, dum dixi, Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem: quando et facto me in agonia, factus est sudor meus sicut guttæ sanguinis decurrentis in terram; Domini recordatus sum; prolixius orando (quæ oratio non est descripta), et dicendo: Pater, si possibile est, aufer a me calicem istum; verumtamen non mea voluntas, sed tua fiat.
paras.en: [[2:8|When my soul was in distress within me|Quum angustiaretur in me anima mea]], when I said, [[Matt 26:38|My soul is sorrowful even unto death|Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem]]: when also, I [[Luke 22:43|being in an agony|facto me in agonia]], my sweat became [[Luke 22:44|as drops of blood, trickling down upon the ground|sicut guttæ sanguinis decurrentis in terram]]; [[2:8|I remembered the Lord|Domini recordatus sum]], by praying the longer (which prayer is not written down), and by saying: [[Matt 26:39|Father, if it be possible|Pater, si possibile est]], take away this chalice from me; [[Luke 22:42|but yet not my will, but thine be done|verumtamen non mea voluntas, sed tua fiat]].

paras.t: Ego autem in voce laudis immolabo tibi sacrificium laudis, secundum quod homo sum. Obtulit etiam Christus Patri vel Trinitati prædam quam de inferis rapuit, dum eam in ascensione Patri præsentavit in patria. Denique, quando in passione immolavit se ipsum, nunquam anima ejus, quoad partem suam superiorem, cessavit a laude divina. Quæcumque vovi, reddam. Sic et nos agere par est. Displicet enim Deo stulta et infidelis promissio, ut Salomon ait.
paras.en: [[2:10|But I with the voice of praise will sacrifice to thee|Ego autem in voce laudis immolabo tibi]] a sacrifice of praise, inasmuch as I am man. Christ also offered to the Father, or to the Trinity, the prey which he snatched from hell, when at the ascension he presented it to the Father in heaven. Lastly, when in his passion he sacrificed himself, his soul, as to its higher part, never ceased from the praise of God. [[2:10|I will pay whatsoever I have vowed|Quæcumque vovi, reddam]]. So too it is fitting that we should do. For [[Eccles 5:3|an unfaithful and foolish promise|stulta et infidelis promissio]] displeaseth God, as Solomon says.
